text.p: - Parliament approved the new cabinet proposed by Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek after almost three months of political uncertainty.
- Foreign exchange reserves at the end of 1996 fell $150 million to $4.1 billion compared to November, the central bank said.
- The blue-chip SBI index rose 2.5 percent on Thursday, ending an eight-day losing streak.
- Ljubljana bourse decided to move the listing of graphic company Cetis to the OTC section of the market instead of on the primary market and postponed the launch to March 10.
- The newly approved government holds its first session on Friday.

- The new government is not much different from the old one, as the prime minister and many new ministers are the same or even worse than before, said Janez Jansa, leader of the biggest opposition party -- Social Democrats.
- Slovenian trading company Merkur opened a franchise shop in the Croatian town of Split only a week after they opened one in Bosnia.
